title: IMS bridge transaction: GU the input message and ISRT the reply to the IO PCB, which the bridge returns to the reply-to queue
shapes: MQBR MQBRMPP: CALL 'CBLTDLI' USING WS-GU IO-PCB WS-IN-AREA, then CALL 'CBLTDLI' USING WS-ISRT IO-PCB WS-OUT-AREA (LL ZZ and text)
asserts: MQBRMPP's ISRT CALL (tagged) is one call_sites fact (CBLTDLI, resolves_to null), a call edge from 1000-REPLY, a gaps entry and one dli_calls fact: function ISRT (from WS-ISRT VALUE 'ISRT'), pcb IO-PCB, io_area WS-OUT-AREA, no ssas. The ISRT to the IO PCB is the call the IMS bridge returns as the reply message.

citations.quote: When an IMS transaction ISRTs to its IOPCB, the message is routed back to the originating LTERM or TPIPE. These are seen in IBM MQ as reply messages.
Reply messages from IMS are put onto the reply-to queue specified in the original message.

notes: The citations document the ISRT-to-IO-PCB reply. The GU of the input message in the same member is a standard DL/I message call that no cited rule covers, so it is not tagged and the key asserts nothing about it for this horror (see H-0097 for a cited DL/I call).
